fable.w: This is a bare definitional provision stating what the term "District" means. One might be tempted to see the District of Columbia as a local government and therefore an outside party, but the section merely defines a term and establishes no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue in connection with any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple definition of a term used in the statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. It merely defines a geographic entity.

opus.w: This section only defines "District" as the District of Columbia. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. Naming a local jurisdiction in a definition does not bring that jurisdiction into any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is purely definitional, establishing the meaning of the term 'District' for the purposes of the statute. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the District of Columbia government) in any federal decision-making process. It merely clarifies terminology.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining "District" as the District of Columbia implies some form of local government involvement or consultation, but this is merely a definitional clause. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision. It simply clarifies a term used elsewhere in the statute.
